dedupe_keys.name: itu ai ml in 5g challenge 5g base station energy consumption dataset huawei 2023

description: This dataset was released for the 2023 5G energy consumption modelling problem of the ITU AI/ML in 5G Challenge, curated by Huawei, to help build machine learning models that predict and reduce the energy use of base stations. It contains measurements from real base stations of several product types, labelled A to D, with their engineering configuration (transmit power, bandwidth, carriers and antennas), cell-level traffic load expressed as allocated resource blocks, the energy-saving methods in use such as symbol and RF shutdown, and the measured energy consumption as the target. Participants trained on a few scenarios and were tested on unseen ones, so the data are split into training and test sets. The files were distributed through the ITU challenge website and the Zindi competition platform, and winning solutions and a later research paper (arXiv 2406.16929) use them. Coverage: an undisclosed set of base stations in commercial networks, hourly records over a limited period. Format and access: CSV files after registering on the challenge or Zindi platform, free; no open licence was found. Caveats: sites, operators and countries are anonymised; availability after the competition is not guaranteed; the licence is unclear. Simulation uses: power models of radio access networks for energy and backup power planning, demand-response and battery sizing at cell sites, and interdependency with electricity supply. Related records: the MIT Supercloud and NLR workload power profiles are the data-centre counterparts.
